headline: SILVER SLAMMED 6%: Precious Metals Post Third Straight Down Week as 30-Year Yield Tops 7% Ahead of FOMC
snippet: Silver tumbled nearly 6% to $64.50 per ounce this week — its third consecutive weekly decline — as stronger-than-expected U.S. PPI data pushed Fed rate-hike odds to 90% on CME FedWatch. Gold settled Friday at $4,347.78, technically up 0.71% on the session but down close to 2% on the week, while the 30-year Treasury yield cracked 7% for the first time in over a year. GoldSeek notes both metals are now in an unusual binary setup heading into the September 15-16 FOMC decision: a hike could trigger long liquidation toward the $4,050-$4,100 support zone, while a hold or dovish surprise would likely spark an outsized short-covering rally above $4,720 resistance. Rising oil prices are compounding the inflationary squeeze and adding pressure on non-yielding assets.

headline: MONTANA MASSIVE SULFIDE GROWING: American Pacific Mining Drills 20.1m of 11.15 g/t Au at Madison — Open to Southwest
snippet: American Pacific Mining (OTC: USGDF) released first 2026 assays from its Madison Copper-Gold Project in Montana on September 9: hole M26C-02 cut 30.8 metres of massive sulfide averaging 7.4 g/t gold, 9.62 g/t silver and 0.29% copper, including a 20.1-metre high-grade interval at 11.15 g/t gold, 14.3 g/t silver and 0.42% copper, and a 7.92-metre sub-interval at 25.33 g/t gold and 0.86% copper. Geological interpretation confirms the massive sulfide body is thickening to the southwest with no prior drilling in that direction — opening a potentially large extension ahead of Phase II drilling of up to 7,500 additional metres planned for fall 2026. Madison sits in a polymetallic VMS-style belt in a jurisdiction with strong access and low political risk.

headline: MOSS GOLD GOING NORTHEAST: Gold X2 Mining Confirms 40.4m of 2.05 g/t Au 2km Beyond Known Deposit Boundary
snippet: Gold X2 Mining (TSXV: AUXX) announced September 8 that its Span Prospect drilling at the Moss Gold Project in Northwest Ontario confirmed a significant northeast extension of the deposit — hole MSD-26-404 returned 40.4 metres grading 2.05 g/t gold from 343.6 metres depth, including 24.05 metres at 3.17 g/t gold. The Span Prospect sits approximately 2 kilometres northeast of the existing deposit boundary, suggesting the Moss Gold system is considerably larger than its current 2.458 million-ounce indicated resource (at 1.04 g/t Au) and 4.209-million-ounce inferred base (at 0.97 g/t Au). The company released an updated NI 43-101 resource estimate simultaneously with the discovery announcement — a rare one-two punch that gives investors a concrete size anchor plus a new open-ended exploration direction.

headline: SONORA MINE RESTART IN PLAY: Goldgroup's 26,000m San Francisco Drill Returns 16.8m at 4.36 g/t Gold in Opening Holes
snippet: Goldgroup Mining (TSXV: GGO; OTC: GORO) released the first six assayed holes from its 26,000-metre drill program at the San Francisco Gold Project in Sonora, Mexico on September 8 — part of a US$8.5 million study evaluating a potential mine restart. Hole GGD-178 cut 16.8 metres at 4.36 g/t gold and 10.0 metres at 2.00 g/t gold; GGD-174 returned 23.4 metres at 1.71 g/t gold; and GGD-179 intersected 51.0 metres at 0.58 g/t gold including 3.9 metres at 2.53 g/t. Results confirm both high-grade intervals and broad mineralized zones consistent with open-pit heap-leach amenability. San Francisco was a producing mine with existing processing infrastructure in place, lowering the capital threshold for restart and making the drilling program an accelerated pre-feasibility study rather than a greenfield exploration campaign.

headline: 724 MILLION TONNES OF COKING COAL: Stanmore Acquires Moranbah South from Exxaro for US$105M, Expanding Queensland Empire
snippet: Stanmore Resources (ASX: SMR) has agreed to acquire 100% of the Moranbah South metallurgical coal tenements in Queensland's Bowen Basin from Exxaro Resources for US$105 million ($145 million AUD), adding 724 million tonnes of measured and indicated Goonyella Middle Seam premium hard coking coal resources immediately adjacent to its existing Eagle Downs and Isaac Downs Extension projects. The strategic fit is significant: Moranbah South's resources could potentially be accessed through Eagle Downs infrastructure if that project advances, reducing capital requirements for development. The acquisition will be funded from existing cash balances with no capital raise required, and closing is targeted before end of Q4 2026, subject to FIRB, ACCC and ministerial tenement transfer approval.

headline: ERIC FIER LEADS C$9M RAISE: CANEX Metals Consolidates Arizona Oxide Gold After Completing Gold Basin Acquisition
snippet: CANEX Metals (TSXV: CANX) completed its 100% acquisition of Gold Basin Resources Corp — folding it in as a wholly owned subsidiary — and simultaneously upsized its strategic financing from C$6.5M to C$9M, with industry veteran N. Eric Fier anchoring the raise with a C$3 million personal commitment. The consolidated Gold Basin/Gold Range Project in Northern Arizona spans mineralized trends exceeding 8 kilometres with multiple known zones and undrilled exploration targets, making it one of the larger advanced oxide gold projects in a permitting-friendly U.S. jurisdiction. Proceeds fund exploration and pre-development at Gold Basin and the company's Louise silver project in British Columbia, plus remaining acquisition obligations. Crescat Capital's involvement in the parallel Westward Gold Nevada financing the same month signals continued institutional interest in western U.S. gold district consolidation plays.

headline: FIRST FINNISS SPODUMENE IN HAND: Core Lithium Hits September Quarter Production Milestone at Recommissioned NT Plant
snippet: Core Lithium (ASX: CXO) has produced its first spodumene concentrate from the recommissioned processing plant at its Finniss Lithium Operation in Australia's Northern Territory — a milestone achieved within six months of the final investment decision and in line with the company's September Quarter 2026 target. Mining at the Grants Open Pit restarted in May, crushing circuits came back online in August, and first concentrate production now confirms the staged restart is on schedule. Core is targeting nameplate production of 1.2 million tonnes per year by mid-2028, with first spodumene shipment planned for December Quarter 2026. The milestone validates the lithium sector's recovery narrative: Finniss was idled during the 2023-2024 price slump, and its return to production — backed by a A$290 million funding package including a Glencore strategic partnership — confirms operator confidence in sustained price strength.

headline: CRESCAT-BACKED NEVADA RAISE: Westward Gold Upsizes Private Placement to C$12M to Drill Cortez and Carlin Trends
snippet: Westward Gold (CSE: WG) upsized its non-brokered private placement from C$5 million to C$12 million — a 140% oversubscription — with lead orders anchored by Crescat Capital LLC and Concept Capital Management Ltd. at a combined C$2.5 million. Proceeds fund ongoing drilling at the flagship Toiyabe Hills Project on the Cortez Trend in Lander County, Nevada, alongside the Coyote and Rossi projects on the Carlin Trend in Elko County. Nevada's Cortez and Carlin Trends have historically produced tens of millions of ounces of gold each, and district-scale juniors with institutional backing in these belts often attract major-company attention during rising gold price cycles. The oversubscription signals strong institutional conviction in Westward's land position ahead of what management expects to be a major drilling season.

headline: SELLOFF OR BREAKOUT: Chris Vermeulen Maps Three Gold Scenarios Ahead of September's Rate Decision Crossroads
snippet: Technical strategist Chris Vermeulen's September 2026 gold analysis for Sprott Money frames precious metals at a genuine inflection point ahead of the September 15-16 FOMC meeting. His primary thesis: gold is completing a Wave 4 corrective structure and the next major move — up or down — will define Q4 2026. A rate hike (now priced at ~90% odds) could push gold toward the $4,050-$4,100 major support zone and flush crowded longs, while a hold or dovish signal would likely trigger a violent short-covering rally above $4,720. Critically, Vermeulen argues the September pullback represents a tactical re-entry opportunity rather than a structural break — central bank demand, sovereign debt dynamics, and de-dollarization provide a durable bid beneath spot prices regardless of near-term Fed outcomes. He flags the current gold-to-S&P ratio as historically consistent with accumulation phases that precede multi-year outperformance by gold miners.

headline: GERMANIUM DEFIES REE SLUMP: Critical Semiconductor Metal Posts +10% Gain in September as Rare Earth Market Flatlines
snippet: The September 2026 rare earth market snapshot records an average change of just +0.31% — but inside that flat headline number, germanium surged +10.04% while scandium fell -7.36%. Germanium's gain stands out: the critical semiconductor metal — used in military infrared optics, fibre optic cables, and thin-film solar cells — is derived primarily as a zinc-smelting byproduct, and China controls roughly 80% of global production. Supply chain concerns linked to U.S. military procurement, combined with tight Western inventories, are driving the bid. For junior mining investors, the germanium surge revives interest in zinc-polymetallic projects with germanium by-product credits, particularly assets outside China with realistic processing pathways. The divergence also underscores that not all rare and critical metals are victims of Chinese oversupply — selectivity within the sector continues to reward investors who distinguish between structurally tight and structurally oversupplied materials.
